report.title: MSE Wall Exclusion - Both End Bents
report.paragraph: D2 I-95 PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE
MSE WALL EXCLUSION BOXES
Both end bents | 13 October 2026 | Minimum setback from pile faces

Solve the wall setback needed for a straight strap, starting on the wall normal through a pile center, to clear that pile within the allowed skew. The red boxes define the MSE back-face exclusion for this arrangement.

c.textvalue: Minimum face clear, nominal pile / zero tolerance

Individual square exclusion box, overall side

report.paragraph: Set the BACK OF FACING outside the red boundary. The rounded box includes the placement allowance; do not add that allowance again. All eight piles use the same live geometry and four-sided face setback. Zero added strap gap is a tangency screen.

report.paragraph: 2. INPUTS AND MINIMUM DISTANCE

The pile width, spacing, count and placement tolerance are live references to the journal geometry. The 3-inch coordinate allowance is applied conservatively in both plan directions. Wall coordinates are a dated CAD snapshot.
Square pile size — shared journal geometry.
Pile spacing along the row — shared journal geometry.

Trial strap width; replace with vendor dimension.
Required clear gap from strap edge to pile; zero is tangency.
Maximum selected skew; ordinary limit 15 deg (SDG 3.13.2.K.8).
Upward rounding increment for the layout box; not added construction clearance.
Conservative pile half-width projected onto wall-aligned axes.

Round UP to the chosen increment; normalize units before native Floor.

Overall individual pile exclusion box side.

DERIVATION: the limiting corner distance normal to the strap is (S − t) sin α − (h + t) cos α. Set this equal to w/2 + c and solve for S. Here h is projected nominal half-width and t is the coordinate allowance. This is derived geometry, not an FDOT prescribed setback.

5. SEPARATE REQUIREMENTS AND USE

c.textvalue: Front cap face to back of front facing

report.paragraph: The pile boxes govern the centered-strap plan clearance. Keep the front face of the cap at least 24 inches from the back of facing as a separate condition. The cap is shown in plan for coordination; it lies above the previous 38-ft trial strap layer.

The 24-inch battered-pile-to-leveling-pad clearance is a different measurement (SDG 3.13.2.N.2.ii). This plan assumes the current plumb piles. Evaluate the whole battered-pile envelope and leveling pad separately if the pile alignment changes.

Outside a box means the wall meets this pile-based setback screen; it does not certify the complete reinforcement route. Check every pile, adjacent wall, connection, reinforcement length, backfill boundary and elevation layer. Ordinary L ≥ max(8 ft, 0.7H), 15° elevation inclination and acute-corner/bin-wall provisions remain separate.

Boxes apply to wall faces parallel to these plan axes, with the centered anchor assumed above. For skewed walls, use pile dimensions projected into the wall axes and recompute. The row rectangle conservatively encloses the union of the four individual boxes.
